title: Pesarattu
jainNotes: Contains ginger. For Jain version, omit ginger and use only green chilli and cumin. Skip onion topping.
recipe: Soak green gram for 3–4 hours. Grind with ginger, green chilli, cumin and salt into a slightly coarse batter (no fermentation needed).
Heat a tawa, pour and spread the batter into a thin crepe. Drizzle oil and cook both sides till crisp.
Serve hot with allam (ginger) pachadi or coconut chutney.
tips: Signature Andhra breakfast crepe – lighter and more protein-rich than regular dosa.
Best eaten fresh and crisp.

title: Rava Upma (Uppindi)
jainNotes: Contains onion and ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion and ginger.

ingredients.name: Onion, green chilli, ginger, curry leaves
Mustard, cumin, urad dal, chana dal

recipe: Dry-roast the rava lightly. Temper mustard, dals, curry leaves, chilli and onion in oil/ghee.
Add water (and vegetables if using), bring to a boil, then add the roasted rava while stirring.
Cook till soft and fluffy. Serve with chutney or pickle.
tips: Everyday Andhra tiffin – made with rava.
A little ghee elevates the flavour.

title: Broken Rice Upma (Uppindi)
jainNotes: Contains onion and ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion and ginger.

ingredients.name: Onion, green chilli, ginger, curry leaves
Mustard, cumin, urad dal, chana dal

recipe: Dry-roast the broken rice lightly. Temper mustard, dals, curry leaves, chilli and onion in oil/ghee.
Add water (and vegetables if using), bring to a boil, then add the roasted broken rice while stirring.
Cook till soft and fluffy. Serve with chutney or pickle.
tips: Everyday Andhra tiffin – made with broken rice.
A little ghee elevates the flavour.

title: Idli with Sambar & Chutney
jainNotes: Traditional sambar contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, use sambar without onion-garlic.

ingredients.name: Toor dal, vegetables (pumpkin, brinjal, drumstick), tamarind, sambar powder

recipe: Steam fermented idli batter in moulds till soft and fluffy.
Prepare a tangy Andhra-style sambar with tamarind, vegetables and sambar powder.
Serve hot idlis with sambar and chutney, often with a sprinkle of karapodi (gunpowder).
tips: Staple South Indian breakfast adapted to Andhra tastes with spicier sambar and podi.
Soft idlis are essential.

title: Pulihora (Tamarind Rice)
jainNotes: Standard hing may contain wheat/gum. Use Jain-certified hing to make it Jain-friendly.

ingredients.name: Mustard, curry leaves, dry red chilli, peanuts, turmeric, hing

recipe: Prepare a thick tamarind paste cooked with turmeric and salt.
Temper mustard, curry leaves, chillies, peanuts and hing in oil. Mix into the tamarind.
Gently mix the tempered tamarind into cooled cooked rice so every grain is coated.
Rest for a while for flavours to develop. Serve at room temperature.
tips: Temple-style tamarind rice – tangy, spicy and aromatic.
A little jaggery balances the sourness.

title: Gongura Pachadi
jainNotes: Contains garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit garlic.

ingredients.name: Garlic, dry red chilli, mustard, cumin

recipe: Wash and roughly chop gongura leaves. Cook or sauté till soft and the sourness mellows.
Temper mustard, cumin, garlic and red chilli in oil. Grind or mash the leaves with the tempering and salt into a coarse chutney.
Serve with rice and ghee or as a side.
tips: Iconic Andhra relish – intensely sour and spicy.
The signature flavour of the state.

title: Tomato Pappu (Andhra Dal)
jainNotes: Contains garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit garlic.

ingredients.name: Mustard, cumin, dry red chilli, curry leaves for tempering

recipe: Pressure-cook toor dal with turmeric and tomato till soft. Mash lightly.
Temper mustard, cumin, garlic, chilli and curry leaves in oil/ghee and pour over the dal.
Serve thick and creamy with rice and ghee.
tips: Classic Andhra tomato dal - thick and robust.
Perfect comfort food with rice.

title: Gongura Pappu (Andhra Dal with Sorrel)
jainNotes: Contains garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit garlic.

ingredients.name: Mustard, cumin, dry red chilli, curry leaves for tempering

recipe: Pressure-cook toor dal with turmeric and gongura leaves till soft. Mash lightly.
Temper mustard, cumin, garlic, chilli and curry leaves in oil/ghee and pour over the dal.
Serve thick and creamy with rice and ghee.
tips: Classic Andhra gongura dal - tangy and robust.
The sourness of gongura perfectly complements the dal.

title: Natu Kodi Pulusu (Country Chicken Curry)
jainNotes: Contains chicken, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Tamarind, red chilli powder, coriander, garam masala

recipe: Marinate chicken with turmeric and salt. Sauté onion, ginger-garlic and chilli till golden.
Add tomato, spice powders and tamarind extract. Cook till oil separates.
Add chicken and simmer till tender and the gravy is thick and spicy.
Serve with rice or ragi sangati.
tips: Fiery Andhra country-chicken curry – tamarind and Guntur chilli define the flavour.
Slow cooking brings out the best taste.

title: Chepala Pulusu (Fish Curry)
jainNotes: Contains fish, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Tamarind, onion, tomato, garlic, red chilli

recipe: Lightly fry fish pieces. Prepare a tamarind-based gravy with onion, tomato, garlic and chilli powder.
Temper mustard, fenugreek and curry leaves. Add the gravy and fish. Simmer gently.
Serve with steamed rice.
tips: Classic coastal Andhra fish curry – tangy, spicy and aromatic.
Do not overcook the fish.

title: Mirchi Bajji
jainNotes: Contains ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit ginger.

ingredients.name: Besan, rice flour, chilli powder, ajwain, ginger-garlic paste, salt

recipe: Slit and deseed chillies if desired. Make a thick besan batter with spices and ginger-garlic paste.
Dip each chilli in the batter and deep-fry till golden and crisp.
Serve hot with onion, chutney or as is.
tips: Iconic Andhra street snack – spicy, crunchy and addictive.
Best eaten immediately.

title: Punugulu
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion.

ingredients.name: Onion, green chilli, curry leaves, cumin

recipe: Mix chopped onion, chilli, curry leaves and cumin into the fermented batter.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry till golden and crisp outside, soft inside.
Serve with coconut or peanut chutney.
tips: Andhra-style deep-fried dumplings from leftover or fresh batter.
Crispy and perfect with evening tea.

title: Gutti Vankaya Kura (Stuffed Brinjal Curry)
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.

ingredients.name: Peanuts, sesame, coconut, spices for stuffing
Onion, tamarind, garlic, chilli powder, oil

recipe: Slit brinjals crosswise without cutting through. Stuff with a roasted peanut-sesame-coconut-spice mixture.
Cook in a tamarind-onion-garlic gravy till the brinjals are soft and the masala coats them.
Serve with rice or roti.
tips: Stuffed brinjal curry – a festive and everyday favourite.
The stuffing should be well-roasted for depth of flavour.

title: Gongura Mamsam (Mutton with Gongura)
jainNotes: Contains mutton, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Cook mutton with onion, ginger-garlic and spices till tender.
Separately cook gongura leaves till soft, then mash or blend.
Combine the gongura with the mutton and simmer till the flavours marry and the gravy thickens.
Serve with rice or roti.
tips: Classic Andhra mutton dish where the sourness of gongura balances the richness of the meat.
One of the most celebrated non-veg preparations of the state.
